newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Oil prices could rise further - former OPEC chief.
newsitem.headline: Oil prices could rise further - former OPEC chief.

text.p: Former OPEC secretary-general Subroto said on Wednesday that higher oil prices were likely if the northern hemisphere winter was severe this year and Iraq was still not able to enter the market.

Subroto told reporters that one reason for a recent surge in oil prices was that inventory levels in industrial countries were low. But he said OPEC, the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries, should ensure some price stability.
"I think OPEC should defend current oil prices, because if prices go higher certainly there will be some pressure to depress them in future," Subroto said.
But he said also the group should maintain its current production ceiling of 25.033 million barrels per day.
"I think OPEC can rise its ceiling if it wants but OPEC would do better to defend its current ceiling. It should watch the market carefully," he said.
Buoyant world oil markets traded near six-year highs on Tuesday after resuming a storming bull run which has carried prices up 40 per cent in the space of four months.
London November futures for international benchmark North Sea Brent blend crude broke above $25 a barrel for the first time since the 1990/91 Gulf War after adding 88 cents on Monday.
